text:
Columbus was the better team by a hair, and it still lost by four. The simulated replays of every shot give CBJ a 51 percent share of deserved wins to 49 for FLA, with CBJ ahead 3.53 to 4.06 in total expected goals only if you count the power plays, and ahead 2.57 to 2.10 at even strength. The difference was special teams. FLA scored on four of six power plays while CBJ went 0 for 2, and the Blue Jackets took 25 penalty minutes to FLA's 6.

Columbus led after a first period it controlled, 1.80 to 0.55 in expected goals, on a Kent Johnson wrist shot at 14:11. Then the second period turned. Brady Tkachuk scored three times, once at even strength and twice on the power play, and Carter Verhaeghe added a power-play snap shot at 17:50 to make it 4-1. Matthew Tkachuk assisted on all four of those goals and finished with five assists without a goal. Cam Talbot allowed 3.48 goals more than the 23 shots against him deserved, and Jet Greaves stopped all four shots he faced in relief.

Sam Reinhart tipped in a power-play goal at 1:20 of the third, and Verhaeghe scored on a 4 percent chance at 3:28 to make it 6-1. Denton Mateychuk and Cole Sillinger scored 22 seconds apart to cut it to 6-3, but Reinhart's snap shot at 17:43 closed it out. Akira Schmid made 24 saves on 27 shots, a tick under what the chances deserved.
